clue.text: Haul put back beside church in valley

indicators.note: put back tells us to read the word for haul from end to start

parts.note: to lug is to haul or drag

explanation.surface: Someone drags a load past a church down in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulch is a narrow, steep-sided ravine, a kind of valley found especially in the American West.

clue.text: Pay-off presumably not going down like a lead balloon?

definitions.text: Pay-off presumably not going down like a lead balloon?

parts.words: Pay-off presumably not going down like a lead balloon?
parts.note: a large severance payment to an executive is golden and lets them float gently down, unlike a lead balloon that drops

explanation.surface: A payoff that is well received, rather than falling flat.
explanation.walkthrough: A metal joke: a lead balloon plummets, while a gold-lined parachute brings a sacked boss down softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous payment guaranteed to a senior executive on dismissal, cushioning their fall from the post.

clue.text: Large misgiving after beheading mammal

indicators.note: beheading means the first letter of the misgiving word is cut off

parts.note: a demur is an objection or misgiving

explanation.surface: Grave doubts about an execution, followed by an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates found in Madagascar, so they are a kind of mammal.

clue.text: Hero of opera in girl's series of operas

parts.note: her means belonging to a girl
the Ring is Wagner's cycle of four operas

explanation.surface: An opera hero appearing in a girl's favourite opera cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Herring is the title role in Britten's comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Herring is the hero of Benjamin Britten's comic opera of that name.

clue.text: Source of wine, mulled, perhaps — peppery stuff?

parts.note: wine is made from grapes
mulled wine is served hot, so mulled is one example of hot

explanation.surface: A recipe note on mulled wine: the grapes, heated and spiced, make a peppery brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peppery stuff?' reads as spice, but grapeshot is small balls fired from a cannon that pepper a target; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot was a cluster of small iron balls fired together, which would pepper an enemy, so it is literally stuff that peppers.

clue.text: Effusiveness upsets son in expression of affection

indicators.note: in places the son abbreviation inside
upsets in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a hug expresses affection

explanation.surface: Over-the-top warmth embarrasses a son receiving a cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gush is an excessive outpouring of feeling, which is what effusiveness means.

clue.text: About to be involved in a commotion over variable old pharmacist

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above the next piece
to be involved in means the about word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: pother is an old word for a fuss or commotion
ca is short for circa, meaning about
Y is a typical algebraic variable

explanation.surface: Someone getting caught up in a fuss over a changeable old chemist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is circa, not a container signal; 'over' in a down clue puts the pieces above the variable.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothecary was a historical maker and seller of medicines, an early pharmacist.

clue.text: Oppose relinquishing initial spirit, one hears

indicators.note: relinquishing initial means giving up the first letter of the oppose word

parts.note: to beard someone is to confront or oppose them boldly
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone opposes giving up their first drink of spirit, so it's heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hears' means one hears with it; to beard is to defy.
explanation.definitionFit: The membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound, the organ by which a person hears.

clue.text: Inept writing possessed by the writer — had to restrict that

indicators.note: to restrict means the had letters hem in what follows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: possessed by means the writing word is held inside the writer word

parts.note: me is how the clue's writer refers to themself
fist is an old word for handwriting

explanation.surface: A clumsy piece of writing, which its author had to keep in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Handwriting was once called a person's fist, so 'writing' is not a manuscript here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham-fisted means clumsy and lacking skill, so it is a close synonym of inept.

clue.text: Limit heatstroke with treatment, getting encouraging response

indicators.note: with treatment means the letters are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor's advice to curb heatstroke by treating it wins approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said in approval when something improves, a typical encouraging response.

clue.text: Meat company importing a lot of hoax wine

indicators.note: importing means the meat and company letters take in the other piece

parts.note: lamb is a meat

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or hoax

explanation.surface: A meat firm caught up in a fraud involving imported wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is a sparkling red wine from the Emilia-Romagna region of Italy.

clue.text: Difficulty entertaining millions with a dance

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest inside, so the difficulty word holds the next letter

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Getting millions to dance together is a real difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom dance of Afro-Cuban origin.

clue.text: Insect was initially found in each fiddle

indicators.note: found in means the first letter sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: to rig is to fiddle or manipulate dishonestly

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word was

explanation.surface: An insect was discovered inside every violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like the instrument but works as the verb to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: The earwig is an insect with pincers at the tail end of its body.

clue.text: Queen to marry in this decade?

indicators.note: in places the queen and marriage letters inside the word this

parts.note: taken as written
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
to tie the knot is to marry, so tie means marry

explanation.surface: Asking whether a queen should wed within this decade.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirties are the decade from 30 to 39 of a century or of a life.

clue.text: Tip of rocket in police cordon possibly evidence of alien visitation?

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the police word

parts.note: a cop is a police officer

indicators.note: tip of means the first letter of rocket

parts.note: a circle is a ring, as a cordon is

explanation.surface: A rocket tip found inside a police cordon hints at an alien landing.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattened patterns in crop fields are sometimes claimed to show that aliens have landed.

clue.text: Father crying sadly about English words of praise

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for English
sadly signals the letters of crying are put in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: A father weeps in sorrow while giving a eulogy in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crying sadly' reads as grief, but 'sadly' reshuffles crying into NGYRIC, and 'about' wraps that round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A panegyric is a public speech or text full of praise, such as a eulogy.

clue.text: Developed for use in a base

indicators.note: developed means the letters are worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: Something built for use at a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a camp, but means morally low.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means wicked or villainous, matching base in its moral sense of low and dishonourable.

clue.text: Transport system satisfied staff will need day off

parts.note: to meet a need is to satisfy it, so met means satisfied

indicators.note: off means the abbreviation for day is taken away from the staff word

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Transport workers, content with their deal, still want a day off.
explanation.definitionFit: A metro is an underground or urban railway network, as in Paris.

clue.text: Would rather, having no power to pass on

indicators.note: having no means the abbreviation for power is removed

parts.note: to prefer is to would rather do something
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Someone without authority would sooner hand the matter on.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer a matter is to pass it on to someone else for a decision.

clue.text: Very much in character, shedding pounds, picking up award

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up means the letters are read upwards
in puts the very much word inside
shedding means the abbreviation for pounds is dropped

parts.note: a letter is a written character
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra
so means very much, as in so tired

explanation.surface: Someone true to type loses weight and wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shedding' drops L from LETTER to give ETTER; SO goes 'in' to make ETTESOR, which 'picking up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge given as a prize, for instance at shows.

clue.text: Some journey to catch good bit of game?

parts.note: part means some of something

indicators.note: to catch means the journey word holds the abbreviation for good

parts.note: a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: A short trip in order to bag a decent piece of game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of game' suggests a portion of a match, but here game means hunted birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a game bird shot in season, so it is one item of game.

clue.text: One's not involved regarding items for detective, seeing twist at the end

parts.note: re means regarding or about

parts.note: a detective looks for clues

explanation.walkthrough: 'twist at the end' swaps the last two letters of CLUES to give CLUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse withdraws from society, so is someone not involved with others.

clue.text: Crime writer to emerge after penning note on chapter

penning means enclosing, so the note goes inside

parts.note: to rise is to emerge or come up
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie was the best-selling English writer of detective fiction.

clue.text: Seafood sensitivity initially affected one

parts.note: camp means exaggerated or affected in manner

clue.text: I damage upcoming resort

parts.note: to maim is to injure or damage

clue.text: Criticise an end to grieving or strong emotion

indicators.note: an end to means the last letter of grieving

explanation.surface: Critics call for an end to mourning or intense feeling.

clue.text: Closer in middle of fun run

indicators.note: middle of means take the central letter of fun

parts.note: to bolt is to run off

explanation.surface: Someone nearer the centre of a charity fun run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closer' reads as nearer, but means something that closes or fastens.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-bolt is a U-shaped bolt with threaded ends used to clamp and fasten things, so it is a fastener.

clue.text: Clot spoiled catalogue

indicators.note: spoiled means the letters of catalogue have been messed up

explanation.surface: A fool has ruined the catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' reads as a noun meaning idiot, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To coagulate is to thicken into a solid mass, as blood does, so it means to clot.

clue.text: Flower, say, brought in for one seasonal gift

indicators.note: brought in means the flower and say pieces go inside the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone brings in a flower as an example of a seasonal present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword favourite for a river, but here it is a plain bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate eggs are given at Easter, a gift tied to that season of the year.

clue.text: Be coming in at six even when kept back

coming in signals the letters sit inside the words at six even
